title: Generalized Matrix Local Low Rank Representation by Random Projection and Submatrix Propagation

problem.claim: The work addresses general matrix local low rank representation, equivalently framed as low rank submatrix detection.

gap.claim: Existing local low rank approximation methods detect only submatrices with specific mean structures and may miss other true and interesting patterns.

contributions.claim: The authors develop RPSP, a random-probing-based submatrix propagation framework for general matrix local low rank representation.
RPSP identifies local low rank patterns by growing them from small low-rank submatrices selected through random projection.
RPSP is supported by random projection theory.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe RPSP as a novel matrix computational framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On synthetic data, the authors report that RPSP outperforms all state-of-the-art methods and robustly and correctly identifies low rank matrices under similar pattern and background means, heteroscedastic noise, and multiple patterns.
On real-world datasets, the authors report that RPSP effectively identifies interpretable local low rank matrices.

narrative_sequence.summary: Matrix low rank approximation reduces statistical redundancy, while local methods can reveal interpretable structures when row-column duality exists.
Local low rank approximation corresponds to low rank submatrix detection, but existing methods are restricted to specific mean structures.
The work introduces RPSP, which uses random projection to find small low-rank submatrices and propagate them into larger local low rank patterns.
The framework is supported by random projection theory and evaluated on synthetic and real-world data.

source_observation.claim: The reported synthetic-data evaluation includes similar pattern and background means, heteroscedastic background noise, and multiple patterns.

interpretation.claim: Evaluation across these conditions suggests that robustness to varied pattern and noise structures is important for local low rank detection.

application.claim: When developing local pattern detection methods, include tests that vary mean contrast, noise heterogeneity, and the number of embedded patterns.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these evaluation conditions cover all practically relevant data regimes.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the random projection theory, algorithmic complexity, or implementation details.
The abstract does not identify the synthetic datasets, real-world datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide formal guarantees or reproducibility details.
